title: The word 'winner': how spammy is it?
hook: A word shows up in most spam. Does that make an email containing it most likely spam?

knows: that a spam filter looks at the words in an email
doesNotKnow: how a word shifts the chance that an email is spam
that how common spam is to begin with (the base rate) still matters

misconception: If a word appears in 60% of spam, an email containing it is 60% likely to be spam.
objective: The learner can count a word's appearances in spam and in real mail to get the chance an email with that word is spam, and explain why the base rate of spam changes the answer.

claims.text: The rates (10% spam; 'winner' in 60% of spam and 10% of real mail) are invented for the toy, labelled 'Invented rates · 100 emails' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 45 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; IN_SPAM, IN_REAL, SHARE_Q in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Of 100 emails at 10% spam, 'winner' is in 6 spam and 9 real emails, so an email with 'winner' is spam 6 out of 15 times: 40%. Real mail outnumbers spam 9 to 1, and the word is 6 times likelier in spam.
With the same word rates, an email with 'winner' is spam 60% of the time at 20% spam, 72% at 30%, 80% at 40% and 86% at 50%.
claims.source: counts(s) in Demo.tsx: 12/20, 18/25, 24/30, 30/35 (0.857). All counts are whole numbers at the slider's steps. node re-run.

claims.text: Naive Bayes spam filters combine word evidence with the base rate of spam using Bayes' rule.
claims.source: About real systems: Sahami, Dumais, Heckerman & Horvitz 1998, 'A Bayesian Approach to Filtering Junk E-Mail', AAAI Workshop on Learning for Text Categorization; Manning, Raghavan & Schütze 2008, Introduction to Information Retrieval, ch. 13 (prior P(c) times word likelihoods).

recall.question: Only 1 email in 100 is spam. A word appears in 90% of spam and 5% of real mail. Is an email containing the word probably spam?
options: Yes, about 90%: the word is in 90% of spam
No: about 1 spam vs about 5 real emails contain it, so roughly 15%
recall.why: Count per 100 emails: 0.9 spam and about 5 real emails contain the word, so 0.9 / 5.85 ≈ 15%. The word raises the odds, but spam is rare to begin with.
